title: Minister Chaudhary pledges to prioritize indigenous issues in climate negotiations - The Rising Nepal
description: Minister Chaudhary pledges to prioritize indigenous issues in climate negotiations  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Antalya (Türkiye), Nov 14: Minister for Agriculture, Forests, and Environment, Geeta Chaudhary, has pledged to strongly advocate for the protection of the rights, identity, culture, and ancestral territories of Indigenous communities affected by climate change.

Speaking at a discussion organized here today by the Nepal Federation of Indigenous Nationalities (NEFIN) on the sidelines of COP-31, Minister Chaudhary emphasized that the impact of climate change and disaster on the territories, culture, and traditional lifestyles of Indigenous communities must be integrated into climate adaptation and development planning.

Noting that she attained her current position as a result of the movements and struggles for inclusion led by Indigenous communities, she reaffirmed her commitment to championing their concerns.

Indigenous activists and representatives participating in the discussion urged that the rights, culture, ancestral lands, and livelihoods of communities affected by climate change be prioritized within international climate negotiations and decision-making processes, including at COP-31.

They pointed out that while the impacts of climate change are intensifying in the Himalayan region, the concerns of the Indigenous communities most severely affected have not been adequately raised on international platforms. They also emphasized that the situation of communities affected by the recent Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi disaster as well as the preservation of their ancestral lands and cultural heritage should be prioritized in Nepal’s climate negotiations.

Participants also stressed that when Nepal raises issues concerning the Himalayan region on international platforms, it should also present the concerns of indigenous nationalities, women, youth, and persons with disabilities in an integrated manner. (RSS)

title: US pretzel chain Auntie Anne’s to open first Nepal outlet on November 21 - The Kathmandu Post
description: US pretzel chain Auntie Anne’s to open first Nepal outlet on November 21  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
American soft pretzel chain Auntie Anne’s is set to open its first outlet in Nepal on November 21, at Bhatbhateni Supermarket in Bouddha, Kathmandu.

The brand is entering the Nepali market through a partnership between its parent company, GoTo Foods, and local distributor JGI Distribution Private Limited. The partners plan to open more outlets in the country in the coming months.

The first outlet will be located on the fourth floor of Bhatbhateni's Food Park and will operate from 10am to 9pm.

Its menu will include freshly baked pretzels in Original, Jalapeño, Cinnamon Sugar, Almond and Pepperoni varieties. Other offerings will include Pretzel Dogs, Pretzel Stix, Mini Pretzel Dogs, dipping sauces and beverages.

The drinks menu will feature lemonade in Original, Peach, Mango and Strawberry varieties, along with hot and cold coffee.

“We are delighted to introduce its freshly baked pretzels and signature experience to Nepal,” said Raj B Shah, managing director of JGI Distribution. He said the Bouddha outlet was the first of several locations the company hoped to develop in the country.

Steven Yang, senior vice-president for Asia-Pacific at GoTo Foods International, said Nepal marked a step in the company's international expansion plans. He said the company was looking forward to expanding the brand through its partnership with JGI Distribution.

Auntie Anne’s was founded in the United States in 1988 and is known for its hand-rolled soft pretzels. Its arrival adds to JGI Distribution's portfolio of international food brands, which already includes Cinnabon and Carvel.

JGI Distribution is part of Jawalakhel Group of Industries, a Nepali consumer goods company with more than 55 years of experience in manufacturing, distribution and brand development.

title: India to launch weekly train between Nepal and Ayodhya — The Hindu - UA.NEWS
description: India to launch weekly train between Nepal and Ayodhya — The Hindu  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
Indian Railways plans to launch a weekly rail service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya in India’s Uttar Pradesh state. The Hindu reports, citing a statement by India’s Ministry of Railways.

A 604-kilometre route

The train route will be approximately 604 kilometres long and will connect Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt station. It will pass through localities in the Indian states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

In addition to the terminal stations, the train will stop at Jainagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

Departures once a week

Services will operate once a week: the train will depart from Janakpur Dham every Saturday and from Ayodhya Cantt every Monday. India’s Ministry of Railways said the new route is intended to strengthen bilateral cooperation through rail connectivity and bring the communities of the two countries closer together.

In June, India and Nepal discussed cross-border rail links, including transport on the Janakpur–Ayodhya route, as well as bilateral cooperation in this field.

title: Nepal Proposes UAE Investment in Budhi Gandaki Hydropower Project - Ratopati
description: Nepal Proposes UAE Investment in Budhi Gandaki Hydropower Project  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal has proposed to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for investment in the Budhi Gandaki Hydropower Project. Nepal made the proposal today during a courtesy meeting in Abu Dhabi between Home Minister Sudhan Gurung, who is on a visit to the UAE, and its Minister of Foreign Trade Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi.

On that occasion, Home Minister Gurung also proposed cooperation in the development of agriculture and service sectors and security technology, his secretariat informed.

Discussions were held between them on various dimensions of bilateral trade, investment, and economic cooperation, as well as on making the security bodies technology-friendly and modern.

Both sides have a positive view on advancing the necessary process by exchanging formal proposals for the projects proposed by Nepal and further strengthening and expanding cooperation in the coming days, the Home Minister's secretariat informed.

Home Minister Gurung had left for the UAE on Friday to participate in the 'World Police Summit' held in Dubai.
